ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which pair of words is a minimal pair for /f/ and /v/? (1 mark)
   A. tin, chin
   B. fine, vine
   C. cat, mat
   D. boy, toy

2. What should you do if a question does not apply to you? (1 mark)
   A. Write a false answer
   B. Tear the form
   C. Write N/A or draw a line
   D. Leave it empty

3. 'As busy as a bee' means (1 mark)
   A. very busy
   B. very lazy
   C. very tall
   D. very quiet

4. In a readers' theatre, learners (1 mark)
   A. sing without words
   B. build a stage from wood
   C. draw pictures only
   D. read a story aloud with different parts

5. What is the plural of 'leaf'? (1 mark)
   A. leaves
   B. leafs
   C. leafes
   D. leaf

6. What is the plural of 'box'? (1 mark)
   A. boxies
   B. boxen
   C. boxs
   D. boxes

7. Which is a linking word that shows something happened at the end? (1 mark)
   A. finally
   B. first
   C. then
   D. next

8. What do we say when someone thanks us? (1 mark)
   A. Congratulations
   B. Excuse me
   C. You are welcome
   D. I beg your pardon

9. Which word has the vowel /eɪ/? (1 mark)
   A. wet
   B. bed
   C. pen
   D. wait

10. In 'bandage', the stress is on (1 mark)
   A. the second syllable
   B. neither
   C. the first syllable
   D. both syllables

11. Which is a good rule for writing an SMS? (1 mark)
   A. Send it to strangers
   B. Use secret code
   C. Leave out your name
   D. Be polite, short and clear

12. Which word begins the greeting in a friendly letter? (1 mark)
   A. Faithfully
   B. Dear
   C. Yours
   D. Sincerely

13. Which word has the short sound /ʊ/? (1 mark)
   A. moon
   B. cook
   C. fruit
   D. spoon

14. What is the comparative form of 'tall'? (1 mark)
   A. taller
   B. tallest
   C. tallr
   D. more tall

15. Which part of a narrative tells how it finished? (1 mark)
   A. The title
   B. The beginning
   C. The ending
   D. The middle

16. Which word helps to show order in a narrative? (1 mark)
   A. table
   B. eleven
   C. blue
   D. suddenly

17. 'Too much sugar is bad for your teeth.' Sugar is (1 mark)
   A. a plural noun
   B. a verb
   C. uncountable
   D. countable

18. Where was Omondi's mother on the day of the story? (1 mark)
   A. At the market
   B. At the clinic getting her medicine
   C. At school
   D. At the barber's

19. When is it fair to interrupt a speaker? (1 mark)
   A. When you are bored
   B. When you did not hear or someone needs urgent help
   C. When you want to talk instead
   D. When you disagree loudly

20. What does 'sanitation' mean? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of food
   B. A type of shoe
   C. Clean toilets, drains and waste systems that protect health
   D. A game

21. What is a factual text? (1 mark)
   A. A joke
   B. A text that gives true information
   C. A poem only
   D. A made-up story only

22. Which of these is a coordinating conjunction? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. but
   C. broom
   D. tidy

23. Which word has the consonant cluster /sk/? (1 mark)
   A. desk
   B. ball
   C. race
   D. goal

24. What is athletics? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of card game
   B. A type of food
   C. Only football
   D. Sports such as running, jumping and throwing

25. In the passage about netball, how many players are in a team? (1 mark)
   A. nine
   B. eleven
   C. five
   D. seven

26. How should you read a poem with rhythm? (1 mark)
   A. Read as fast as you can
   B. Whisper every line
   C. Tap the beat and stress the strong syllables
   D. Skip the rhymes

27. What is the past participle of 'eat'? (1 mark)
   A. eaten
   B. eated
   C. ate
   D. eating

28. In which word is the letter b silent? (1 mark)
   A. baby
   B. bus
   C. debt
   D. bag

29. Which word ends with the sound /ŋ/? (1 mark)
   A. sing
   B. sun
   C. sum
   D. sin

30. Which is the correct spelling of the colour of a ripe banana? (1 mark)
   A. yelllow
   B. yelow
   C. yellow
   D. yeloww

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Rewrite with correct capital letters and full stops: 'we visited lake victoria in august' (3 marks)

32. What is a nonverbal cue? Give two examples. (3 marks)

33. Write three ways to make your speech clearer. (3 marks)

34. Write two reasons why people keep diaries. (2 marks)

35. Explain why we say 'a university' but 'an umbrella'. (3 marks)

36. State two things you can find in a dictionary entry. (2 marks)

37. Write two words that contain /ɛə/, two that begin with /j/ and one that has /ʒ/. (5 marks)

38. Write two similes about food. (2 marks)

39. Write four sentences about your family. Use a, an and the at least once. (4 marks)

40. State three materials you can read for pleasure. (3 marks)

41. Change to negative statements: (a) She sells eggs. (b) They picked coffee. (4 marks)

42. Write two sentences using a simile of your own about a celebration. (4 marks)

43. Write the -ing form of: run, sit, swim. (3 marks)

44. Explain the difference between a common noun and a proper noun. Give one example of each. (3 marks)

45. Fill in with a, an or the: 'Mama bought ___ cabbage and ___ egg. ___ egg was big.' (3 marks)

46. Explain what the proverb 'Many hands make light work' means and give an example. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — fine, vine
   Fine and vine differ only in the first sound, /f/ and /v/.

2. C — Write N/A or draw a line
   N/A means not applicable and shows that you did not forget.

3. A — very busy
   Bees always seem to be working, so it means very busy.

4. D — read a story aloud with different parts
   Each reader takes a part and reads the lines.

5. A — leaves
   Change f to ves.

6. D — boxes
   Nouns ending in x add es.

7. A — finally
   Finally introduces the last event.

8. C — You are welcome
   You are welcome is the polite reply.

9. D — wait
   Wait has /eɪ/, but wet, pen and bed have /e/.

10. C — the first syllable
   We say BAN-dage.

11. D — Be polite, short and clear
   A good SMS is clear and polite.

12. B — Dear
   Friendly letters begin with Dear and the name.

13. B — cook
   Cook has /ʊ/.

14. A — taller
   Short adjectives add er.

15. C — The ending
   The ending gives the result.

16. D — suddenly
   Time words show order.

17. C — uncountable
   We cannot count sugar one by one.

18. B — At the clinic getting her medicine
   The story says she was at the clinic.

19. B — When you did not hear or someone needs urgent help
   Only interrupt for good reasons, and do so politely.

20. C — Clean toilets, drains and waste systems that protect health
   Sanitation protects health by keeping waste away.

21. B — A text that gives true information
   Factual texts share facts.

22. B — but
   'But' joins words or sentences.

23. A — desk
   'Desk' ends in sk.

24. D — Sports such as running, jumping and throwing
   Athletics includes track and field events.

25. D — seven
   The passage says two teams of seven players.

26. C — Tap the beat and stress the strong syllables
   Follow the beat with your voice.

27. A — eaten
   Eat, ate, eaten.

28. C — debt
   'Debt' is said 'det'.

29. A — sing
   'Sing' ends with /ŋ/.

30. C — yellow
   Yellow has a double l.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: We visited Lake Victoria in August.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for We, 1 mark for Lake Victoria and August, 1 mark for the full stop.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: A nonverbal cue is a message sent without words. Examples: a smile shows happiness; a thumbs-up shows approval.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 for each example.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Open your mouth enough; speak slowly at first; listen to a good model and copy them; practise every day.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: To remember events; to practise writing; to record feelings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Both start with the letter u, but university starts with the consonant sound 'yoo', so it takes a. Umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so it takes an. We choose by sound, not by letter.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each example and 1 mark for the sound rule.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any two: spelling, meaning, part of speech, example sentence, pronunciation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: /ɛə/: chair, care. /j/: yellow, young. /ʒ/: television.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: The bread was as soft as a pillow. The juice was as sweet as honey.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: I have a brother. He has an old bicycle. The bicycle is red. We ride it in the yard.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence that uses the articles correctly.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Story books, poems, magazines, comics, newspapers (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: (a) She doesn't sell eggs. (b) They didn't pick coffee.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks each: 1 for the correct helping verb, 1 for the base form of the main verb.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: The cake was as sweet as honey. The children danced like leaves in the wind.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each sentence with a correct simile.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: running, sitting, swimming
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: A common noun is a general name such as 'town'. A proper noun is the special name of one person, place or thing, such as 'Kisumu', and begins with a capital letter.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for both examples.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: a, an, The
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct article.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: It means a job is easier when many people help. For example, the whole class can sweep the compound quickly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 1 for a suitable example, 1 for clear expression.
